cases.name: policy_trace_reactor_ascent_to_scram
cases.note: The oracle's 900-step reactor trace (godot/scripts/nova/conformance.json, reactor_trace): reactor_rules.nova driven by the scripted rod program, faults off, 0.05 s per tick, through STARTUP, POWER ASCENSION, STEADY and OVERHEAT to an automatic SCRAM. Inputs are the plant's, recorded from the Python reference host; the host's own inputs (scram, scram_elapsed, game_over, victory, meltdown) are computed by the host model.

# ==========================================================================
# reactor_rules.nova -- reactor control policy, in NovaLang
#
# This file is the reactor's brain. Trip setpoints, alarm tiers, the
# fault injector and the operating-state machine all live here, and
# nothing else does: the core integration is reactor_physics.py, the
# panel is Godot. Edit this file and the plant behaves differently on
# the next run -- no Python change, no Godot rebuild.
#
# Read each tick from the host (do not `set` these):
#   t, dt                      seconds since start, step size
#   flux_pct                   neutron flux, 100 == rated power
#   fuel_temp_c, mod_temp_c, out_temp_c, pressure_mpa
#   reactivity_pcm             total reactivity this step
#   rod_a, rod_b               actual bank positions, % withdrawn
#   scram                      is the plant currently latched in SCRAM
#   scram_elapsed              seconds since the trip (0 if not scrammed)
#   operator_scram             the big red button, this tick only
#   game_over                  run has ended (meltdown or victory)
#
# Written back to the host: everything in `effects`, plus state,
# rod_target_a/b, and the scram()/meltdown()/victory()/alarm()/log()
# actions.
# ==========================================================================

reactor "CHERNOBYL-1" version 1

params {
    # ---- protection setpoints ----
    trip_flux_pct         = 150.0     # neutron flux high trip
    trip_flux_sustain_s   = 1.0       # flux must stay above trip_flux_pct
                                       # this long before it actually
                                       # scrams -- filters a brief prompt-
                                       # kinetics spike (fuel/moderator
                                       # negative feedback often turns one
                                       # of these around on its own within
                                       # a second) from a real runaway
    trip_fuel_temp_c      = 800.0     # fuel temperature high trip
    trip_pressure_mpa     = 18.5      # primary overpressure trip
    trip_lowflow_frac     = 0.5       # loss-of-flow trip, above trip_lowflow_power_pct
    trip_lowflow_power_pct = 50.0

    # ---- alarm thresholds (advisory tier) ----
    warn_flux_pct         = 115.0
    # 550/650/800/1200 (warn/overheat/trip/meltdown) replace the original
    # 1200/1500/1800/2800: steady 100% rated power only ever settles
    # around 416 C given this plant's own heat-transfer constants (see
    # reactor_physics.gd's HTC_FUEL_MOD/HTC_MOD_OUT), so the old
    # thresholds sat 3-7x hotter than the plant could realistically
    # reach even during a real excursion. These keep the same relative
    # spacing/escalation the original had, just anchored to what this
    # plant can actually do -- see reactor_theme.gd, core_grid.gd and
    # core_heatmap.gdshader, which all mirror these same four numbers
    # for their own color scales and must be rescaled together with this.
    warn_fuel_temp_c      = 550.0
    warn_pressure_mpa     = 17.5

    # ---- damage / win conditions ----
    meltdown_temp_c       = 1200.0
    meltdown_sustain_s    = 5.0
    overheat_temp_c       = 650.0
    startup_flux_pct      = 3.0
    ascension_flux_pct    = 60.0
    survive_time_s        = 900.0     # 15 minutes on shift and you win

    # ---- post-trip cooldown ----
    scram_cooldown_s      = 600.0

    # ---- fault injector timing ----
    fault_first_min_s     = 45.0
    fault_first_max_s     = 90.0
    fault_gap_min_s       = 45.0
    fault_gap_max_s       = 90.0

    # ---- xenon ----
    xenon_max_pcm         = 400.0
    xenon_ramp_s          = 60.0

    # ---- optional autopilot (0 = manual, the default) ----
    auto_rod_control      = 0.0
    auto_target_power_pct = 100.0
    auto_rod_gain         = 0.010
}

# Values faults drive. Anything not marked `persistent` snaps back to its
# default at the top of every tick, so a fault that clears stops acting on
# the plant with no explicit cleanup.
effects {
    flow_frac       = 1.0
    load_frac       = 1.0
    stuck_bank      = ""
    xenon_pcm       = 0.0   persistent
    stuck_bank_pick = "A"   persistent
}

# Derived each tick, before any rule runs.
signals {
    power_ok      = flux_pct < warn_flux_pct and fuel_temp_c < warn_fuel_temp_c
    thermal_slack = meltdown_temp_c - fuel_temp_c
    hot           = fuel_temp_c > overheat_temp_c
    running       = not game_over

    # ---- protection channel votes ----
    # A real trip system never scrams off one instrument -- a single stuck
    # or noisy sensor should not be able to drop the plant. Each channel
    # below is independent (flux, fuel temp, primary pressure, coolant
    # flow); flux_trip's held() debounce still filters a brief prompt-
    # kinetics spike, same as before. See protection_trip.
    flux_trip     = held(flux_pct > trip_flux_pct, trip_flux_sustain_s)
    fuel_trip     = fuel_temp_c > trip_fuel_temp_c
    pressure_trip = pressure_mpa > trip_pressure_mpa
    lowflow_trip  = flow_frac < trip_lowflow_frac and flux_pct > trip_lowflow_power_pct
    trip_votes    = flux_trip + fuel_trip + pressure_trip + lowflow_trip
}

# ==========================================================================
# PROTECTION -- highest priority, these run before anything else
# ==========================================================================

rule operator_scram priority 300 edge {
    when  operator_scram and running
    then  scram("MANUAL SCRAM INITIATED")
}

# 2-out-of-4 coincidence: no single channel may scram the plant alone, so a
# lone stuck sensor (or one brief real excursion) cannot trip it -- two
# independent channels have to agree first. Real plants vote trips the same
# way for exactly this reason.
rule protection_trip priority 290 {
    when  running and not scram and trip_votes >= 2
    then  let reasons = []
          if flux_trip     { reasons = append(reasons, "NEUTRON FLUX HIGH") }
          if fuel_trip     { reasons = append(reasons, "FUEL TEMPERATURE HIGH") }
          if pressure_trip { reasons = append(reasons, "PRIMARY OVERPRESSURE") }
          if lowflow_trip  { reasons = append(reasons, "LOSS OF COOLANT FLOW") }
          scram("AUTO SCRAM -- 2-CHANNEL COINCIDENCE: " + join(reasons, " + "))
}

# ==========================================================================
# END OF RUN
# ==========================================================================

rule core_disassembly priority 200 once {
    when  running and held(fuel_temp_c > meltdown_temp_c, meltdown_sustain_s)
    then  meltdown("CORE DISASSEMBLY -- MELTDOWN")
          alarm(3, "MELTDOWN")
}

rule shift_survived priority 195 once {
    # held(), not a raw t >= survive_time_s -- t is the plant's total
    # elapsed clock and never resets on its own, so a straight time check
    # let an operator get scrammed, sit tripped for the rest of the
    # shift, and still win once the clock ran out. held(not scram, ...)
    # only counts CONTINUOUS scram-free time and drops back to zero the
    # instant a trip happens (see nova_evaluator.gd's _eval_held()), so a
    # SCRAM now genuinely costs the whole shift's progress, not just the
    # power excursion that caused it.
    when  running and held(not scram, survive_time_s)
    then  victory("15 MINUTES SURVIVED -- VETERAN OPERATOR")
}

# ==========================================================================
# ALARMS -- highest level raised in a tick wins
# ==========================================================================

rule alarm_meltdown_imminent priority 150 {
    when  running and fuel_temp_c > meltdown_temp_c
    then  alarm(3, "CORE TEMPERATURE CRITICAL")
}

rule alarm_overheat priority 145 {
    when  running and hot and fuel_temp_c <= meltdown_temp_c
    then  alarm(2, "CORE OVERHEATING")
}

rule alarm_flux priority 140 {
    when  running and flux_pct > warn_flux_pct
    then  alarm(2, "NEUTRON FLUX HIGH")
}

rule alarm_pressure priority 135 {
    when  running and pressure_mpa > warn_pressure_mpa
    then  alarm(2, "PRIMARY PRESSURE HIGH")
}

rule alarm_fault priority 130 {
    when  running and active_fault != ""
    then  alarm(1, fault_label)
}

rule warn_flux_entry priority 125 edge {
    when  running and flux_pct > warn_flux_pct
    then  log("CAUTION: FLUX ABOVE 115%")
}

rule warn_temp_entry priority 124 edge {
    when  running and fuel_temp_c > warn_fuel_temp_c
    then  log("CAUTION: FUEL TEMPERATURE ABOVE 550 C")
}

# ==========================================================================
# OPERATING STATE -- guards are mutually exclusive, so order is irrelevant
# ==========================================================================

rule state_meltdown priority 60 {
    when  not running and not victory
    then  set state = "MELTDOWN"
}

rule state_victory priority 59 {
    when  not running and victory
    then  set state = "SECURED"
}

rule state_scram priority 58 {
    when  running and scram
    then  set state = "SCRAM"
}

rule state_overheat priority 57 {
    when  running and not scram and hot
    then  set state = "OVERHEAT"
}

rule state_startup priority 56 {
    when  running and not scram and not hot and flux_pct < startup_flux_pct
    then  set state = "STARTUP"
}

rule state_ascension priority 55 {
    when  running and not scram and not hot
          and flux_pct >= startup_flux_pct and flux_pct < ascension_flux_pct
    then  set state = "POWER ASCENSION"
}

rule state_steady priority 54 {
    when  running and not scram and not hot and flux_pct >= ascension_flux_pct
    then  set state = "STEADY"
}

# Once decay heat has died away the trip is cleared and the operator gets
# the rod drives back. Until then the sliders are dead and the rods stay in.
rule cooldown_complete priority 50 edge {
    when  scram and running and scram_elapsed >= scram_cooldown_s
    then  reset_trip()
          log("REACTOR COOLDOWN COMPLETE -- ROD DRIVES RESTORED")
}

# ==========================================================================
# XENON -- keeps decaying after the poisoning fault clears
# ==========================================================================

rule xenon_recovery priority 20 {
    when  active_fault != "xenon_poisoning" and xenon_pcm < 0.0
    then  set xenon_pcm = min(0.0, xenon_pcm + (xenon_max_pcm / xenon_ramp_s) * dt)
}

# ==========================================================================
# OPTIONAL AUTOPILOT -- set auto_rod_control = 1 in params to enable
# ==========================================================================

rule auto_regulate priority 10 {
    when  auto_rod_control > 0 and running and not scram
    then  set rod_target_a = clamp(rod_target_a + auto_rod_gain * (auto_target_power_pct - flux_pct) * dt, 0.0, 100.0)
          set rod_target_b = clamp(rod_target_b + auto_rod_gain * (auto_target_power_pct - flux_pct) * dt, 0.0, 100.0)
}

# ==========================================================================
# FAULT INJECTOR
#
# One fault is active at a time. The engine picks by weight, keeps the
# body running every tick for `duration` seconds, logs "ALARM: <label>"
# on entry and "<label> CLEARED" on exit, then waits fault_gap_min_s..
# fault_gap_max_s before the next one.
# ==========================================================================

fault turbine_trip weight 1.0 duration 120.0 label "TURBINE TRIP" {
    set load_frac = 0.0
}

fault feedwater_failure weight 1.0 duration 45.0 label "FEEDWATER PUMP FAILURE" {
    set flow_frac = 0.3
}

fault rod_stuck weight 1.0 duration 35.0 label "CONTROL ROD BANK STUCK" {
    set stuck_bank = stuck_bank_pick
}

fault xenon_poisoning weight 1.0 duration 60.0 label "XENON POISONING" {
    set xenon_pcm = 0.0 - xenon_max_pcm * ramp(fault_elapsed / xenon_ramp_s)
}

# The bank a stuck-rod fault seizes is latched once, on the rising edge of
# the fault, so it cannot flicker between A and B while the fault runs.
rule latch_stuck_bank priority 95 edge {
    when  active_fault == "rod_stuck"
    then  set stuck_bank_pick = pick("A", "B")
          log("BANK " + stuck_bank_pick + " DRIVE SEIZED")
}

host_calls: scram(AUTO SCRAM -- 2-CHANNEL COINCIDENCE: FUEL TEMPERATURE HIGH + PRIMARY OVERPRESSURE)
